advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether the partially-generated docs/ticket-model.md must be registered in docs/generated-artifacts.md and the generated-surface marker registry, and reconcile with the 'new generator MUST be added to both' contract.
evidence: docs/ticket-model.md:13: `<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_ticket_model_taxonomy.py; do not edit by hand. -->`
tests/unit/test_generated_surface_markers.py:38 comment: '#: A new generator MUST be added here and to the generated-artifact catalog together.'
GENERATED dict (test_generated_surface_markers.py:39-55) lists config-reference/env-vars/etc. but NOT docs/ticket-model.md
ABSENCE: search for 'gen_ticket_model_taxonomy' returns no hit in docs/generated-artifacts.md; the catalog's Generated files table (lines 11-19) omits ticket-model.md
advisory.finding: docs/ticket-model.md now carries a generated banner and a marker-delimited generated block, but it is not registered in the generated-surface catalog docs/generated-artifacts.md nor in the GENERATED registry in tests/unit/test_generated_surface_markers.py, unlike every other generator-backed doc (config-reference.md, env-vars.md, etc.). The repo's own contract states 'A new generator MUST be added here and to the generated-artifact catalog together.'

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert the source-drift fixture actually differs from the source (e.g. verify str.replace changed the text) so the drift test cannot silently degrade to a no-op if types.py reformats the TicketStatus literal.
evidence: test hardcodes: `'TicketStatus = Literal["idea", "open", "in_progress", "blocked", "closed", "archived", "deleted"]'`
src/rebar/types.py:21: `TicketStatus = Literal["idea", "open", "in_progress", "blocked", "closed", "archived", "deleted"]`
source.replace(...) has no assertion that a substitution actually occurred, so a non-match silently yields an unmodified fixture
advisory.finding: test_check_mode_fails_when_source_vocabulary_changes_without_regeneration hardcodes a byte-exact copy of the TicketStatus Literal (types.py line 21) and injects drift via str.replace of that literal. If types.py reformats that line (e.g. black wraps the Literal across lines), the replace matches nothing, no 'triaged' member is added, and the test asserts returncode==1 on an unchanged fixture — a false expectation coupled to source formatting rather than to the vocabulary itself.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a docs/generated-artifacts.md catalog row for docs/ticket-model.md naming source `src/rebar/types.py` and regenerate command `python scripts/gen_ticket_model_taxonomy.py`.
evidence: docs/ticket-model.md:13: `<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_ticket_model_taxonomy.py; do not edit by hand. -->` establishes a new generated documentation surface derived from src/rebar/types.py

docs/generated-artifacts.md:3: 'This catalog identifies checked-in generated files ... Correct a generated file through the source and regeneration command listed below.' — the catalog owns generated-file ownership and regeneration; search for `ticket-model.md` in this file returned no matches
tests/unit/test_generated_surface_markers.py:38: '#: A new generator MUST be added here and to the generated-artifact catalog together.' proves the catalog must gain a row for a new generator
advisory.finding: docs/ticket-model.md now contains a generated taxonomy block produced by scripts/gen_ticket_model_taxonomy.py (banner at line 13, derived from src/rebar/types.py), but the generated-artifacts catalog docs/generated-artifacts.md is not updated to list this new generated surface, its source, and its regeneration command.
scenarios: A contributor hand-edits the taxonomy block in docs/ticket-model.md and cannot find its source/regeneration path because the catalog omits it
An operator consults docs/generated-artifacts.md to learn which docs are generated and misses ticket-model.md
advisory.suggested_fix: In docs/generated-artifacts.md 'Generated files' table, add a row: `docs/ticket-model.md` (the generated taxonomy block) | the canonical `TicketType`/`TicketStatus` Literals in `src/rebar/types.py` | `python scripts/gen_ticket_model_taxonomy.py` | its enforcing drift gate.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add tests driving `_replace_generated_block` on a markerless legacy document (regex path), on a markerless doc with only the idea heading (fallback path), and on a doc missing the idea heading (RuntimeError).
evidence: scripts/gen_ticket_model_taxonomy.py:97 `replaced, replacements = _LEGACY_TAXONOMY_RE.subn(generated_block + "\n", document, count=1)`
scripts/gen_ticket_model_taxonomy.py:101-104 idea-heading fallback and 'cannot place ticket taxonomy block' RuntimeError

Every test starts from the committed doc which already has markers: tests/unit/test_gen_ticket_model_taxonomy.py:66 `shutil.copyfile(DOC, sandbox_doc)` (DOC contains BEGIN/END markers per docs/ticket-model.md:12,41), so the legacy/fallback branches are unreachable in tests.

ABSENCE: no test constructs a markerless document containing 'A ticket is one of …' + '## The `idea` status' to drive the legacy regex, nor a markerless doc missing the idea heading to assert the RuntimeError.
advisory.finding: The legacy-migration branches of `_replace_generated_block` (the `_LEGACY_TAXONOMY_RE` substitution at lines 97-99 and the idea-heading fallback / missing-heading RuntimeError at lines 101-104) are never exercised: every test copies the already-migrated committed doc, which contains the BEGIN/END markers, so `_replace_generated_block` always takes the `begin_count == 1` branch (line 90). The one-time migration from the old hand-maintained 'A ticket is one of five types…' prose — the stated purpose of this change — has zero coverage.
scenarios: A future regen against an un-migrated doc, or a regression in the legacy regex, ships undetected.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test that builds a synthetic doc from the pre-change prose ('A ticket is one of five types … \n\n## The `idea` status …'), runs `main(['--doc', sandbox])`, and asserts the generated block replaced the legacy text while preserving surrounding prose; plus a test asserting RuntimeError when neither markers, legacy text, nor idea heading are present.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert the rendered table rows appear in exact `get_args(TicketType)`/`get_args(TicketStatus)` order and that the emitted counts equal `len(get_args(...))`.
evidence: Contract in added output: scripts/gen_ticket_model_taxonomy.py:72 `f"There are {len(ticket_types)} canonical ticket types, in declaration order:\n"`
Test asserts membership only: tests/unit/test_gen_ticket_model_taxonomy.py:48-51 `for ticket_type in get_args(rebar_types.TicketType): assert f"`{ticket_type}`" in doc`
ABSENCE: no assertion compares the rendered row sequence to `get_args(...)` order, and no assertion checks the emitted count number matches `len(get_args(...))`.
advisory.finding: The generated output declares the tables are 'in declaration order' and states counts ('There are 7 …'), but no test asserts order or count — `test_committed_taxonomy_block_lists_every_live_type_and_status` uses only membership checks (`f"`{ticket_type}`" in doc`). A regression that reorders the rendered rows relative to Literal declaration order, or emits the wrong count, would still pass every test.
scenarios: `_markdown_table` or `get_args` iteration order changes; a sorted() creeps in; count/list desync.
advisory.suggested_fix: Extract the rows between the two table headers and assert `rows == [f"| `{v}` |" for v in get_args(...)]`, and assert `f"There are {len(get_args(rebar_types.TicketType))} canonical ticket types" in doc`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add tests passing a `--types` file that (a) omits TicketType/TicketStatus and (b) defines an empty Literal, asserting exit 1 with the respective RuntimeError message.
evidence: scripts/gen_ticket_model_taxonomy.py:51-52 `except AttributeError as exc: raise RuntimeError(f"{types_path} must define TicketType and TicketStatus")`
scripts/gen_ticket_model_taxonomy.py:53-54 `if not ticket_types or not ticket_statuses: raise RuntimeError(... must be non-empty Literals)`
ABSENCE: the only `--types` override test (test_check_mode_fails_when_source_vocabulary_changes_without_regeneration) supplies a valid drifted types file, never a malformed/empty one.
advisory.finding: The `_load_types` error paths added in this diff are untested: the AttributeError→RuntimeError guard for a types module missing `TicketType`/`TicketStatus` (lines 51-52) and the non-empty-Literal guard (lines 53-54) never run in any test. A named violating input — a `--types` file defining neither Literal, or defining `TicketType = Literal[()]` (empty) — would exercise these but is never supplied.
scenarios: types.py refactor drops or renames a Literal; the error message contract silently changes.
